tasks.short: Assign polish, symmetry and clarity grades.

steps.what: Examine actual stones and assign polish, symmetry and clarity grades using established systems
inputs: actual stone
actual grading-system criteria
actual inspection instruments
outputs: actual chosen polish, symmetry and clarity grades

steps.what: Enter and check actual assigned grades in the gem grading system {OTHER}
inputs: actual chosen polish, symmetry and clarity grades
actual stone identifier and grading-system version
outputs: checked final actual stone grade entry

steps.what: Commit the checked final actual stone grade entry
inputs: checked final actual stone grade entry

tasks.design: Configure existing stone-reference and grading-system fields in the gem grading system {OTHER}. The worker examines the actual stone, chooses all grades and checks the final entry before committing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Grade recording can repeat stone and grading-system references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native selected-stone context can reduce exact reference entry.
tasks.still_hard: Polish, symmetry and clarity assessment require actual examination and grading judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognises borderline features and applies the actual grading criteria.
tasks.altitude: Less grade-reference entry; grading remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native stone-reference fields can reduce grade-entry repetition; they do not determine actual gem grades.

assumptions: Worker creates actual grade decisions in s1 and enters/checks them in retained s2; existing inventory supplies actual stone identifier only. No vision grading or free judgement capture is assumed.

Only an existing grade record is included. Absent records are omitted and shares reweighted; no additional certificate-writing baseline is invented. Clarity plots are separately covered by task 15096 and counted once.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native context first; already configured entry earns zero saving. Routine commit retains one percent and uses the existing final entry check.
unknowns: Which stone references are actually retyped?
Are all grade fields already native?
research_questions: Can existing stone context reduce record entry without reducing examination?

incremental.description: Maintain actual stone-reference and grading-version fields.

approvals.approved_version: s2 checked final actual grade entry and exact stone destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 9*0.20 reference entry = 1.8; minus 0.5 upkeep = 1.3. Half eligible gives 0.9 minus 0.5 = 0.4. Examination, actual grade choice and commit remain retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify and plot stone clarity characteristics.

steps.what: Identify actual stones' clarity characteristics through examination
inputs: actual stone
actual inspection equipment
actual clarity plotting conventions
outputs: actual observed clarity features and positions

steps.what: Document stones' clarity characteristics using native plot diagrams in the grading tool {OTHER}
inputs: actual observed clarity features and positions
actual stone shape, orientation and identifier

steps.what: Check final clarity diagram against actual observed features and stone orientation
inputs: draft actual clarity plot diagram
actual observed clarity features and positions

steps.what: Save the checked final actual clarity plot
inputs: checked final actual clarity plot

tasks.design: Configure native stone outlines, symbols and reference fields in the gem plotting tool {OTHER}. The worker examines the stone, supplies actual feature positions and checks the final plot before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clarity plots can repeat outline drawing, symbols and stone references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native shape templates and plotting symbols can reduce repeated drawing.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising real inclusions and their orientation requires gem examination.
tasks.human_edge: The worker distinguishes actual internal features from surface effects or misleading views.
tasks.altitude: Less diagram construction; inclusion identification stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native gem plot templates and symbols can reduce diagram construction; they do not identify inclusions automatically.

assumptions: Worker identifies actual features in s1 and captures feature type, position, orientation and stone identifier within retained s2. No image interpretation, free feature extraction or generated inclusion is assumed.
Cuts cover repeated outline/symbol/reference work, not actual feature capture or examination. Native plot functions first; existing templates earn zero saving.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Full final plot verification remains retained; save is one percent and uses that existing check. Any external certificate delivery is a separate actual gated send.
unknowns: Which diagram work is still repeated manually?
Are native plotting symbols already used?
research_questions: Do native plot aids reduce drawing after actual feature capture and orientation checks?

incremental.description: Maintain actual plot templates and symbol conventions.

approvals.approved_version: s3 checked final actual clarity plot and exact stone destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.40 plot construction = 8; minus 1 upkeep = 7. Half eligible gives 4 minus 1 = 3. Identification, feature capture, final check and save remain retained.

tasks.short: Estimate wholesale and retail gem values.

steps.what: Retrieve and verify actual pricing guides and relevant current market evidence
inputs: actual stone identification and assessed characteristics
actual authorised pricing sources
actual relevant market observations
outputs: checked relevant pricing and market sources

steps.what: Choose applicable guide comparisons and actual wholesale or retail valuation adjustments
inputs: checked relevant pricing and market sources
actual stone condition and economic context
outputs: actual chosen valuation inputs, adjustments and uncertainty

steps.what: Calculate draft wholesale and retail value estimates from actual chosen inputs
inputs: actual chosen valuation inputs, adjustments and uncertainty
actual verified quantity, weight and currency units
outputs: calculated draft wholesale and retail estimates

steps.what: Check final estimated gem values against actual stone and market evidence
inputs: calculated draft wholesale and retail estimates
actual chosen valuation inputs, adjustments and uncertainty
outputs: checked final actual gem valuation record

steps.what: Save the checked final actual gem valuation record
inputs: checked final actual gem valuation record

tasks.design: Configure native pricing-source links and fixed valuation arithmetic in the gem valuation tool {OTHER}, using actual source documents in {DOCS}. The worker selects applicable comparisons and adjustments, checks the final estimates and saves the existing valuation record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Valuation can repeat source navigation and arithmetic after judgement inputs are selected.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source links and fixed calculation fields can reduce those operations.
tasks.still_hard: Market relevance, stone quality and appropriate wholesale/retail adjustments require expert judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognises when a guide comparison is inappropriate for the actual stone or transaction context.
tasks.altitude: Less pricing navigation and arithmetic; valuation judgement stays human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native price-source links and fixed arithmetic can support a chosen gem valuation; they do not establish current market prices or select suitable comparisons.

assumptions: Actual authorised guide/market sources supply date, currency, grade/size band and quoted basis; worker verifies in s1 and selects actual comparisons, weight/quantity, conversion basis and adjustments in s2. Missing values remain manual; no current prices are asserted here.
No free stone grading or market appraisal is assumed. S3 removes arithmetic only; s4 retains full economic and stone-specific review.

Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Native source/calculation functions first; existing automatic formulas earn zero saving. Only an existing valuation record is included; no new certificate or sale baseline is invented.
Routine save retains one percent and uses the existing final estimate check. Any external valuation delivery or transaction is a separate actual gated action with no saving claimed here.
unknowns: Which source navigation and calculations are actually manual?
Are guide inputs usable under existing access?
research_questions: Can native links/formulas reduce preparation after full comparison and adjustment judgement?

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final actual gem valuation record and exact stone destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.50 navigation + 20 arithmetic = 30; minus 1.5 upkeep = 28.5. Half eligible gives 15 minus 1.5 = 13.5. Actual valuation choices, final review and save remain retained.

tasks.short: Advise customers on using gems in attractive jewellery.

steps.what: Retrieve and check actual gem specifications and relevant jewellery examples
inputs: actual customer question
actual available gem characteristics
actual relevant jewellery examples
outputs: checked relevant gem and jewellery context

steps.what: Advise customers and others on best gem use for attractive jewelry items
inputs: checked relevant gem and jewellery context
actual customer preferences and constraints
outputs: actual gem-use advice and customer questions

tasks.design: Configure native selected-stone links in the gem inventory system {OTHER} and relevant example links in {DOCS}. The worker checks source relevance and personally advises the customer about attractive and practical gem use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice can repeat navigation to actual stone specifications and examples.
tasks.enabler_now: Native selected-stone and example links can shorten lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Taste, durability and appropriate jewellery use require personal discussion and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The worker understands the customer's preferences and the actual stone's visual character.
tasks.altitude: Less source lookup; customer advice remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native stone/example links can reduce advice preparation; they do not choose attractive gem use for a customer.

assumptions: Actual inventory supplies existing stone characteristics and actual example owner supplies images/specifications. Worker checks relevance in s1 and learns actual preferences in s2; no free new specification or design is assumed.
Boundary is lookup and oral advice. No record write, report, custom design drawing or digital send is required by the stated task; actual additional duties must be decomposed before estimating them.
Shares are provisional, not measured baselines. Only actual repeated navigation is eligible; existing native links earn zero saving.
unknowns: How often is actual specification/example lookup needed?
research_questions: Can native source links reduce preparation without changing customer discussion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 10*0.40 navigation = 4; minus 0.5 upkeep = 3.5. Half eligible gives 2 minus 0.5 = 1.5. All actual customer advice remains retained.
